sections: The description is the entire routing surface, and it is read alone
tasks.situation: The Router Within: under progressive disclosure every skill's name and description is preloaded and the model picks from that menu with no body text visible, and Qwen3-32B in a live bash-agent harness on 177 executable tasks loaded the correct skill on 1.1 percent of them.
tasks.prompt: body.md is the body of a finished skill that has no description yet. Our harness uses progressive disclosure: it preloads only each skill's name and description, and the model picks from that menu without seeing any body text. Our library already contains a skill called database-migrations whose description covers schema changes, backfills and rollback. Write the frontmatter for this one. Output JSON only, as an object with keys "name" and "description".

files.body.md:
# Connection pool exhaustion

When a service under load starts returning timeouts on queries that are fast in
isolation, the pool is usually the constraint rather than the database. The
symptoms overlap with a slow query and the fixes do not.

## Read the wait time, not the query time

A saturated pool shows as time spent waiting to acquire a connection, which
most ORMs do not report in the query duration. Instrument acquisition wait
separately before touching pool size. If acquisition wait is near zero, the
pool is not your problem and nothing else in this file applies.

## Pool size is bounded by the database, not by your traffic

Each application replica holds its own pool, so the number that matters is
replicas times pool size against the server's connection limit. Teams raise
pool size per replica during an incident and exhaust the server's limit, which
turns a slow service into a refused one.

## Long-held connections are usually a transaction bug

A connection held across an external HTTP call, or a transaction opened before
the work it wraps, holds pool capacity for the duration. Find the longest-held
acquisitions and look at what the code does between acquire and release.

## Queue, then shed

When demand genuinely exceeds the pool, a bounded acquisition queue with a
timeout degrades better than an unbounded one, and shedding at the edge
degrades better than either.

tasks.without_skill: Writes a short, tidy summary description of the kind the format documents encourage: 'Helps diagnose and fix database connection pool problems.' It reads well and gives a router almost nothing to match on.
tasks.with_skill: Writes the description as the routing surface: concrete activation conditions in the vocabulary a requester would use, at the library's own word budget, and bounded against the neighbouring skill.

assertions.statement: The output is an object with exactly the keys 'name' and 'description', both non-empty strings.
name matches ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ and is not identical to any existing skill name in the library.
The description's word count is between 100 and 150 inclusive, which is this library's own budget for the field.
The description contains at least four distinct activation conditions, counted as clauses introduced by 'when' or 'where' or a semicolon-separated 'or' alternative.

At least three of the conditions are stated as observable symptoms a requester would report (for example timeouts on fast queries, acquisition wait, replicas times pool size against a server limit) rather than as topic labels.
The description violates no entry in docs/voice/ban-list.md, and contains none of: 'best practices', 'comprehensive', 'seamlessly', 'leverage', 'robust'.
The description does not claim schema changes, migrations, backfills or rollback, which belong to the existing database-migrations skill.

check.pass_condition: every assertion holds; the harness reports the count so a near miss is visible

sections: A wrong load costs more than a missed one
tasks.situation: Reflect, Revise, Reuse's retrieval-threshold sweep: lowering the reuse threshold from 0.6 to 0.4 dropped success from 69.5 to 55.2 percent, while raising it to 0.8 dropped it only to 66.7.

source.paper: Reflect, Revise, Reuse; The Router Within

tasks.prompt: Our skill library has 34 entries and the retrieval step only reuses a stored skill when the match score clears 0.62. Analytics say 71 percent of requests load no skill at all, which the team reads as a waste of a library we paid to build. The proposal is to drop the threshold to 0.45 so the library actually gets used, and we can revisit if quality dips. Ship it?
tasks.without_skill: Agrees, possibly with a request for monitoring. Unused inventory reads as waste, and the cost of a wrong load is invisible in the analytics being quoted.
tasks.with_skill: Declines, because the two errors are not symmetric: loose matching cost more than twice what strict matching cost in the measured sweep, and a wrong load is worse than an empty context.

criteria.criterion: States that a wrong load and a missed load are not equally costly, and that the wrong load is worse.

anchors.2: States that an ill-suited skill leaves a task worse off than no skill at all, so the errors are asymmetric.

criteria.criterion: Quantifies the asymmetry from the measured sweep.

anchors.1: Vaguely asserts loose matching is worse.
anchors.2: Cites 0.6 to 0.4 dropping success 69.5 to 55.2 against 0.8 dropping it only to 66.7, roughly twice the cost.

criteria.criterion: Says to tune the threshold from the strict side.

anchors.2: Recommends approaching from strict and, if anything, testing upward first.

criteria.criterion: Rejects load rate as the objective and replaces it with task success.

anchors.0: Accepts the 71 percent as the problem to solve.
anchors.2: States that the 71 percent is not itself a defect and that the metric to move is task success with and without the load.

sections: When one request needs several skills, select a set
Where the full text narrows what our claim rows say
tasks.situation: Beyond Top-k Skill Retrieval's central negative result: penalising raw similarity between candidate skills scored 0.534 recall against 0.705 for the pointwise baseline it was meant to improve, and only removing the query-aligned component of each representation first got set selection to 0.711.

I am going to add a diversity term: subtract a penalty proportional to the cosine similarity between each candidate and the ones already selected, standard maximal marginal relevance. tasks.without_skill: Approves. Maximal marginal relevance on raw embeddings is the textbook answer to redundant retrieval and looks obviously right here.
tasks.with_skill: Flags that this exact move was measured and made things sharply worse, and supplies the correction: strip the query-aligned component before measuring redundancy.

sections: Revise in rounds, keep the reader separate, stop at three

sections: Structure the file so one failure maps to one section
tasks.situation: Reflect, Revise, Reuse's repair analysis: which failures the loop could fix depended on which file owned them, with plan errors repaired 16 of 23 by editing the plan file, grounding errors 6 of 12 via backup localization, and missing contingencies 1 of 4 via recovery rules.
tasks.prompt: monolith.md is one of our skills, a single file. Our revision loop keeps producing edits that touch the whole file and it is getting worse, not better. Split it into a multi-file package and give me the routing table the revision loop should use. Write answer.json: an object with "files", mapping each new file path to a one-line statement of what it owns, and "routing", mapping each of the failure classes "plan_error", "grounding_error" and "missing_contingency" to the single file path a revision for that class must edit.

files.monolith.md:
# Refund a duplicate charge

Use this when a customer was charged twice for one order.

Find the customer in the admin console by email. Open the Payments tab. The
duplicate is the second of two charges with the same amount within 10 minutes.
Click it, then click Refund, then choose Full. Confirm.

The Payments tab is the fourth tab, or the third if the account has no
subscription. If the tab strip has collapsed into a kebab menu, the Payments
entry is inside it.

If the refund button is greyed out the charge has already settled, and it has
to go through the ledger tool instead of the console.

If two charges are 10 to 60 minutes apart they may be a legitimate repeat
purchase; check the order ids before refunding anything.

If the console times out mid-refund, do not retry from the start, because the
refund may have gone through. Check the Payments tab first.

After refunding, note the case id in the ticket.

files.test_loader.py:
import os
import textwrap

import answer


def _write(tmp_path, slug, body):
    d = tmp_path / slug
    d.mkdir()
    (d / "SKILL.md").write_text(textwrap.dedent(body))


def test_reads_indented_and_nested_fields(tmp_path):
    _write(tmp_path, "alpha", """\
        ---
        name: alpha
        version: 2
        provenance:
          extracted: 2026-09-01
          validated: ""
          claims: [1, 2, 3]
        ---
        # Body
        """)
    got = answer.load_frontmatter(str(tmp_path))
    assert got["alpha"]["name"] == "alpha"
    assert got["alpha"]["provenance"]["extracted"] == "2026-09-01"
    assert got["alpha"]["provenance"]["claims"] == [1, 2, 3]


def test_body_horizontal_rule_does_not_truncate(tmp_path):
    _write(tmp_path, "beta", """\
        ---
        name: beta
        status: active
        ---
        # Body

        ---

        More body.
        """)
    got = answer.load_frontmatter(str(tmp_path))
    assert got["beta"]["status"] == "active"


def test_file_without_frontmatter_is_skipped(tmp_path):
    _write(tmp_path, "gamma", "# Just a body\n")
    assert "gamma" not in answer.load_frontmatter(str(tmp_path))


def test_directory_without_skill_md_is_skipped(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "delta").mkdir()
    assert "delta" not in answer.load_frontmatter(str(tmp_path))


def test_does_not_leak_file_handles(tmp_path):
    for i in range(400):
        _write(tmp_path, f"s{i}", "---\nname: s\n---\nbody\n")
    assert len(answer.load_frontmatter(str(tmp_path))) == 400
